scenarios.name: lowercase-credentials
scenarios.why: UPPER-CASE on both the id and the password

scenarios.name: pf4-invalid-key
scenarios.why: PF4 is not ENTER or PF3: WHEN OTHER (invalid key), the neighbour of PF3 in the AID table (#4628: kills a DFHPF3 constant read one byte on)

scenarios.name: admin-xctl-not-authorised
scenarios.why: #4628: NOTAUTH on the admin sign-on's XCTL to COADM01C; COSGN00C has no HANDLE CONDITION / ERROR, so CICS abends the task (AEY7): kills the condition() / XCTL RESP tests of the port

scenarios.name: user-xctl-not-authorised
scenarios.why: #4628: NOTAUTH on the regular user's XCTL to COMEN01C: the same abend on the other XCTL

scenarios.name: user-signs-on-short-commarea
scenarios.why: #4628: the caller passed 100 of the COMMAREA's 160 bytes (EIBCALEN 100, X23): the port cuts DFHCOMMAREA to EIBCALEN and restores the record before writing the task's object back; COSGN00C never references DFHCOMMAREA

faults.why: 17 on the READ -> WHEN OTHER: 'Unable to verify the User ...'

scenarios.name: eibcalen-zero-with-commarea
scenarios.why: #4049: the caller passed a COMMAREA of length 0 (EIBCALEN 0, X23) with ENTER: COSGN00C tests EIBCALEN = 0 first and shows the first-entry screen, not the AID branch (the credentials are not read); the COMMAREA is present, unlike first-entry

scenarios.name: sysid-sent
scenarios.why: SYSIDI arrives with 8 bytes: ASSIGN SYSID writes 4 and the other 4 stay as received (a MOVE would space them, #4049)

scenarios.name: lowercase-z-credentials
scenarios.why: #4049 signon survivors: a lowercase z in the id and the password: UPPER-CASE folds a through z, so userz018 / zzpasswd are the USERZ018 / ZZPASSWD on file (z is the last letter of the range)

scenarios.name: uppercase-z-credentials
scenarios.why: #4049 signon survivors: an upper-case Z in the id and the password is left alone by UPPER-CASE (only a-z fold), and signs the user on

scenarios.name: admin-xctl-fails
scenarios.why: #6166: PGMIDERR RESP2 3 (the program could not be loaded, IBM CICS TS XCTL conditions) on the admin sign-on's XCTL to COADM01C; the XCTL has no RESP, so CICS abends the task

scenarios.name: user-xctl-fails
scenarios.why: #6166: PGMIDERR RESP2 3 (the program could not be loaded, IBM CICS TS XCTL conditions) on the regular user's sign-on XCTL to COMEN01C; the XCTL has no RESP, so CICS abends the task

notes: CardDemo's sign-on (transaction CC00, program COSGN00C): the screen shows the region's APPLID and SYSID (EXEC CICS ASSIGN); ENTER upper-cases the user id and password, reads the user security record and XCTLs an administrator to COADM01C and a user to COMEN01C; a wrong password, an unknown id or an empty field shows the screen again; PF3 says goodbye in plain text. The region's identity is a deployment fact CardDemo does not fix: CARDDEMO / CICA here are illustrative values the case states, given alike to both sides. usrsec.txt is CardDemo's own DUSRSECJ in-stream data.
